featured_reviews.name: rajesh vaishnav
featured_reviews.review_text:
GUUD Auto House & Works

I had a highly disappointing and distressing experience at GUUD Auto House & Works, located around 6:30–7 p.m. during my visit.

Upon entering the shop, I interacted with a man who appeared to be the owner, Gurupreet Narang. I inquired about a rain cover for my bike, and instead of offering help or guidance, he responded in a highly inappropriate and unprofessional manner. When I asked whether the cover was truly necessary or if the bike could endure the rain, he made a sarcastic remark questioning whether I had received the bike as a gift or through family. This was both personal and unnecessary.

Even before I could complete my questions about whether a cover might affect the look of the bike, he said the bike would look unpleasant even when I sat on it. This was a deeply insulting comment.

Later, I asked to see mobile holders for the bike. He showed me two options, but I politely declined them as they didn’t meet my needs. He reacted arrogantly, dismissing my opinion and insisting that my preferences were “useless.” Then he made an uncalled-for remark comparing the situation to disobeying a father’s advice and learning only after failure. I found this completely unprofessional and personally inappropriate.

Throughout the interaction, he used religious expressions like "Waheguru Stanam" while simultaneously making derogatory remarks—something I found deeply offensive and irreverent.

Additionally, he was seated in very casual attire that I believe was not appropriate for a customer-facing business setting. His tone throughout was condescending, sarcastic, and dismissive—not just with me, but as I observed, with other customers as well.

Although I had initially come prepared to make purchases, including a rain cover and seat cover, the behavior and attitude I encountered compelled me to leave without buying anything.

As someone who also runs a business, I believe every customer deserves basic respect and professionalism, even if they don’t make a purchase. This experience was a stark contrast to that principle.
